page: Microsoft Azure D2ns_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs originating from a single physical Intel Xeon 8573C core operating at up to 4.2 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity is set to 8.0 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes modern vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions (amx_tile and amx_int8), alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration like VAES and SHA-NI. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached remote storage, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance paired with constrained aggregate throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2101.0, placing it in the top 25% of tested environments due to its high clock speed. However, because the instance relies on a single dual-threaded physical core, multi-threaded workloads scale marginally. The multi-core Geekbench score is 2590.0, and multi-core stress-ng tests fall into the bottom 10%. Memory throughput benchmarks reflect similar constraints, with uncached large-block read speeds measuring 17.21 GB/sec and write speeds at 12.81 GB/sec, leading to subdued results in memory-bound tests such as PassMark memory and Redis SET operations.

The D2ns_v6 is best applied to workloads where individual thread execution latency matters more than aggregate parallel throughput. Appropriate use cases include lightweight web serving, application middleware, small-scale microservices, orchestration agents, and development or testing environments. Systems demanding high concurrent multi-threading, substantial in-memory caching throughput, or intensive local I/O should target instances with multiple physical cores and bundled NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ns_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Supported by 8.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio without bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Architectural highlights include hardware support for AVX-512, Intel AMX, and accelerated cryptography. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score in the top 25%, offset by weak multi-core and memory bandwidth results stemming from its single-core hyperthreaded topology. With remote Premium Storage capability and no included public IPv4 addresses, the instance offers balanced entry-level compute efficiency. It is well suited for lightly threaded microservices, small API backends, task runners, and continuous integration agents.
